topic: Utilities: AI as reliability and flexibility lever
angle: Treat AI like grid planning: portfolio bets, reliability SLAs, and frontline adoption, not lab demos.
sourceTitle: Utilities at an inflection point: Four strategic evolutions ahead
linkedinPost:
Utilities aren’t software companies—until grid reliability and flexibility force them to behave like one.

A recent McKinsey piece argues European utilities face a structural reset: electrification, renewables volatility, and AI will redefine the operating model and economics. Translation: more decisions move from monthly planning cycles to near‑real‑time software loops.

My take from the front lines: treat AI like grid planning, not like an app. Build a portfolio of use cases with reliability SLAs, not one flashy pilot. Examples that pay back: demand forecasting to shave peak purchases, outage triage that routes the right crew the first time, and customer communications that cut calls during storms.

The unlock isn’t model accuracy alone—it’s frontline adoption. Dispatchers must trust recommendations. Field techs need workflows that work offline. Regulators need explainability.

Measure business outcomes, not “AI activity”: SAIDI/SAIFI reduction, forecast error vs. spot price avoided, truck rolls and call volume deflected, and time-to-restore.

If you run a utility or an energy retailer, what’s the one reliability KPI you’d be willing to put in an AI contract as a performance target? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy #CustomerExperience
xPost: Utilities don’t need more AI pilots—they need reliability SLAs. Tie AI to SAIDI/SAIFI, peak buys avoided, and truck rolls reduced. Treat it like grid planning, not an app demo. #EnterpriseAI #AIStrategy
